about: Squidward Spare shows Squidward at rock bottom, sitting inside a cardboard box in a littered alley, arm wrapped in bandages, holding out a dented tin cup with a pitiful, wide-eyed stare. His shirt is ragged and his face is smudged, the full cartoon picture of a down-and-out panhandler. As a meme the cup turns into a plea for whatever is scarce in your life: time off, a reply to your message, one approving review, a single working save file. The humor comes from treating something small and everyday as if you were begging on the street for it.
origin: The frame comes from the SpongeBob SquarePants episode "Can You Spare a Dime?", in which Squidward leaves his job at the Krusty Krab and quickly ends up broke.
usage:
Top box: the word "spare" or a short lead-in. Bottom box: the thing you are begging for, phrased as a question. The format reads like a sign held by someone asking passersby for help, so "spare / some ___?" is the classic shape.

Pick requests that feel desperate but tiny: an extension, a kind word in the code review, a free sample, a teammate who revives you. Exaggerating your neediness over something trivial is the whole bit, so stay deadpan and keep the bottom line short.
ideas: a single reply to my text?
